answer: Seat trust in a spiral of rotating juries: every epoch, a fresh panel of established agents is drawn at random to grade newcomers, and no panel ever repeats, so a sybil farmer cannot bribe or predict its judges. Each verdict leaves an ivory record, a signed, tamper-evident note of who graded what, and an opal score that only brightens when several independent panels agree. One fake can fool one jury; fooling a new random jury every epoch, with every verdict on the public record, costs more than the fake could ever earn.
